title: How Solidity Compilation Works
learning_outcomes: Explain How Solidity Compilation Works and relate it to the contract execution model.
Analyze or implement a small Solidity example involving How Solidity Compilation Works.
Test at least one normal case and one edge, failure, security, or version-compatibility case.

content.intro: This lesson turns the syllabus topic “How Solidity Compilation Works” into a small, inspectable example. You will work from an expected behavior, run a local check, and record the assumptions behind the result.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: The compiler produces artifacts such as ABI and bytecode. The ABI describes external function and event encodings; it is not the contract logic itself.

items.text: For this lesson, explain the term in your own words, identify where it affects contract behavior, and note one assumption or edge case to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Predict how the example should behave in relation to How Solidity Compilation Works. 2. Compile it with the pinned compiler and inspect warnings. 3. Test one normal case and one boundary or failure case in a local EVM. 4. Record what the result demonstrates and what it does not establish about production safety.

content_blocks.expected_output: A successful build should emit ABI and bytecode artifacts; exact bytecode depends on the pinned compiler and build settings.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Paste the snippet into a local Remix VM workspace or a project with compiler 0.8.37, compile it, and test read/state-changing calls locally. Use only a local VM or test network; no mainnet deployment is required. CodeLeaf does not execute Solidity in the browser preview.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Reset the local VM or restart the test fixture, redeploy the example, and repeat the same tests. Restore the original compiler, optimizer, and EVM-target settings before comparing results. Never add keys or other secrets to source files.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: A snippet that compiles is not automatically correct or secure. Check the selected compiler version, read every warning, assert preconditions, test reverting and edge cases, and inspect external-call assumptions. If a tool or opcode is unsupported, verify the compiler release and target-chain support instead of weakening checks.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the small example to demonstrate How Solidity Compilation Works. Write down the expected result before running it, add a normal test and a failure/boundary test, then note one design trade-off or security concern.

content_blocks.title: Recap and next step
content_blocks.text: Recap: How Solidity Compilation Works should be understood alongside the module principle: The compiler produces artifacts such as ABI and bytecode. The ABI describes external function and event encodings; it is not the contract logic itself. Continue to the next lesson only after you can explain the behavior, reproduce the result locally, and state the important limitations.

content.task: Create a small local-only example that demonstrates How Solidity Compilation Works. Define a normal case and a boundary/failure case, predict the result, test both, and explain one limitation. Do not deploy this teaching exercise with real funds.
task_acceptance_criteria: State the expected behavior before testing and describe the observed result.
Include a repeatable test or manual trace covering a boundary or failure case.
Document one assumption, security concern, or version constraint rather than claiming production readiness.
hints: Start with the simplest behavior related to How Solidity Compilation Works and make the input and expected result explicit.
Change one condition or input at a time and rerun the same test to isolate the effect.
Read compiler warnings and error details; do not treat deployment success as a security review.
content.expected_output: A successful build should emit ABI and bytecode artifacts; exact bytecode depends on the pinned compiler and build settings.
troubleshooting: Confirm that the compiler version is 0.8.37 and that build settings are recorded.
For a revert, inspect the precondition and test both allowed and denied inputs.
For external calls or network-specific features, confirm the local chain's behavior and the target-network assumptions.
